| hero | H1 School Cleaning Standards | "School cleaning standards decide whether a campus stays safe and inspection-ready – this guide maps the requirements a Victorian business manager verifies before scoping a program." | c-h1 |
| definition | H2 What are school cleaning standards? | "School cleaning standards are the hygiene and amenity requirements a school keeps across classrooms, toilets, corridors and canteens – the duties a school documents and a contractor delivers on schedule." | c-b01 |
| provenance | H2 Where the requirements come from | "The requirements come from Department of Education guidance, the school's own spec and public health advice – three layers that stack, not one document." | c-b02 |

| duties | H2 The duties a school cleaner carries | "A school cleaner's duties run vacuum, mop, sanitise amenities, empty bins and wipe touch points in a set zone order. Responsibilities extend past the mop: the cleaner is the person who sees the campus at its emptiest, so the role quietly absorbs reporting duties too." | c-b04 |
| steps | H2 What are the 6 basic cleaning steps in a school? | "The six steps run wash, wipe, rinse, dry, check and sign – the same surface loop every zone repeats." | c-b05 |
| cadence | H2 Do janitors clean classrooms every day? | "Yes – janitors clean classrooms every school day, typically after hours once students and staff have left." | c-b06 |
| titles | H2 What is a cleaner at a school called? | "A school cleaner is called a cleaner, custodian or facilities officer – the title changes, the duty set does not." | c-b07 |
| hours | H2 How many hours does a school need per week? | "A school's weekly hours are set by enrolment and building size – the roster is specified per zone, not bought as a lump; a service provider prices against that roster." | c-b08 |

### Proof items (term lists, verbatim)

| Item | Type | cid |
|---|---|---|
| "Hygiene – which surfaces carry germ risk between students and how often each is treated." | card | c-b01 |
| "Amenity – whether toilets, corridors and shared rooms stay usable through the day." | card | c-b01 |
| "Evidence – which records prove the work ran, so a complaint or inspection has an answer." | card | c-b01 |
| "Education guidance – the department's facilities expectations: safe buildings, usable amenities and hygienic shared spaces." | card | c-b02 |
| "School spec – the campus's own task list: rooms, frequencies, products and the sign-off chain the principal's office keeps." | card | c-b02 |
| "Public health advice – outbreak and hygiene guidance that changes with seasons and events." | card | c-b02 |
| "Contract clause – the requirement that lands in the cleaner's agreement; everything above collapses into clauses the contractor must meet." | card | c-b02 |
| "Classrooms – desks, chair tops, teacher surfaces and floor areas; the highest-volume zone on campus." | card | c-b03 |
| "Amenities blocks – student toilets, basins, dispensers and urinals; the zone with the strictest hygiene line." | card | c-b03 |
| "Corridors and stairs – floors, handrails and lockers; traffic areas that collect soil all day." | card | c-b03 |
| "Gym floors – sports courts and equipment rooms; dust, sweat marks and floor-finish care." | card | c-b03 |
| "Canteens – food-service surfaces, sinks and floors; cleaning rules closer to a kitchen than a classroom." | card | c-b03 |
| "Admin zones – office desks, reception and staff rooms; standard office duties at school hours." | card | c-b03 |
| "Zone order – cleanest to dirtiest: teaching rooms and admin first, amenities blocks last, so a cloth never travels backwards." | card | c-b04 |
| "Bins – room bins emptied, relined and moved to the collection point on the school's waste day." | card | c-b04 |
| "Touch points – door furniture, railings, switches and shared equipment wiped on the daily pass." | card | c-b04 |
| "Reporting – damage, graffiti and spills beyond routine scope logged for the business manager's morning review." | card | c-b04 |
| "Wash – detergent lifts soil; skipping this step locks dirt under disinfectant." | step | c-b05 |
| "Wipe – the disinfectant pass, contact time observed." | step | c-b05 |
| "Rinse – residue removed on food-contact and desk surfaces." | step | c-b05 |
| "Dry – moisture removed so the next treatment is not diluted." | step | c-b05 |
| "Check – a visual pass against the spec line for that zone." | step | c-b05 |
| "Sign-off – the rota entry that turns the pass into evidence." | step | c-b05 |
| "Tidy routines – teaching rooms end the day with chairs up and floors clear so the evening pass reaches every surface." | card | c-b09 |
| "Lunch supervision – yard duty keeps food waste inside eating zones instead of corridors." | card | c-b09 |
| "Waste systems – enough bins, emptied before they overflow, placed where students actually use them." | card | c-b09 |
| "Spill reporting – a named person who hears about a spill or mess before it becomes a hazard." | card | c-b09 |

### FAQ Q&A pairs

| Q | A | cid |
|---|---|---|
| What are the recommended guidelines for school cleaning? | For business managers the answer is the school's own duty list – areas, frequencies, products and sign-off – built on Department of Education guidance and current health advice. | c-b11 |
| What are the duties of a school cleaner? | Vacuum, mop, sanitise amenities, empty bins and wipe touch points in zone order, plus damage and spill reporting. | c-b11 |
| What is a cleaner at a school called? | Cleaner, custodian or facilities officer – the tasks are defined by the spec, not the title. | c-b11 |
| Do janitors clean classrooms every day? | Yes – every school day, typically after hours, with touch-point disinfection on the same loop. | c-b11 |
| What are the 6 basic cleaning steps? | Wash, wipe, rinse, dry, check and sign – the surface loop every zone repeats. | c-b11 |
| What is the 1 minute rule for cleaning? | If a task takes under a minute – a spill, a dropped wrapper, a smear on glass – do it now rather than logging it; on a school rota the day porter owns that window. | c-b11 |
| What is the 5-5-5 rule for cleaning? | A declutter habit that sorts a room into keep, donate and remove – useful for storerooms and lost-property shelves, while the spec names the clutter zones everywhere else. | c-b11 |
